om-namah-shivaya.brief: Oṃ; homage to Śiva. The mantra addresses and honours Śiva; Trika invites us also to discover that the one invoking is not ultimately separate from the invoked.
om-namah-shivaya.logic: Treat this as offering the next moment, not requesting a special sensation.
om-namah-shivaya.howto: When: At a threshold: standing up, leaving a room, or noticing that attention has become scattered. Practice: Say the entire mantra once, at a normal pace. A slight bow of the head is enough; no counting is required. Return: Do the next ordinary thing carefully.
om-namah-shivaya.sign: Everyday integration: Do the next ordinary thing carefully.

_editorial.needs_check: Do not break namaḥ into naḥ·maḥ; the five-syllable count is na–ma–śi–vā–ya, preceded here by oṃ.

bah-gayatri.brief: The Gāyatrī asks that Aghora direct or inspire understanding. The epithet koṭarākṣa needs a secure gloss from the textual tradition.
bah-gayatri.logic: The act is asking for guidance, not proving that a deity has intervened.
bah-gayatri.howto: When: When you deliberately want to begin a devotional recitation, not as an emergency shortcut. Practice: Recite it calmly once, or three times if following the supplied ritual sequence. Do not require breath holds or body sensations. Return: Return to the task with a more careful intention.
bah-gayatri.sign: Everyday integration: Return to the task with a more careful intention.

_editorial.pocket_iast_candidate: oṃ bahurūpāya vidmahe koṭarākṣāya dhīmahi tan no ’ghoraḥ pracodayāt
_editorial.needs_check: CHECK source spelling bahurūpāya (long ū), and the meaning of koṭarākṣa; do not print the unsubstantiated “hundred-thousand-eyed” gloss.

bahurupa-core.brief: These verses extol the capacity of sacred recitation to remove affliction and wrongdoing. Such benefits are claims of the tradition, not verifiable clinical effects.
bahurupa-core.logic: Entrust the problem to Bhairava while remaining ready to act responsibly in the world.
bahurupa-core.howto: When: For a deliberate period of prayer, rather than in a queue. Practice: Read the complete source-verified three-verse passage, without pressure to memorise all of it. If a brief line is chosen later, label it as an extract, not a mantra. Return: Address what can be addressed; seek practical help where needed.
bahurupa-core.sign: Everyday integration: Address what can be addressed; seek practical help where needed.

_editorial.needs_check: HOLD: supplied numbering/content do not match another available Bahurūpa-Garbha recension; collate Academy PDF before publication. Not genuinely pocket length.

bahurupa-close.brief: This close praises the efficacy of the mantra and the importance of reciting even when ritual procedure has been imperfect. Its superlative claims are internal to the hymn.
bahurupa-close.logic: Let the ritual finish without obsessively asking whether it was flawless.
bahurupa-close.howto: When: At the end of a deliberate ritual or an evening recitation. Practice: Recite the verified complete passage. If using the short phrase, remember it is a context-dependent assertion about this hymn, not a universal standalone invocation. Return: Put away the materials, and continue the evening.
bahurupa-close.sign: Everyday integration: Put away the materials, and continue the evening.

mpa-1.brief: Homage to the One whose form is the universe, yet who is beyond its manifest forms.
mpa-1.logic: The room need not become extraordinary; it is included in what is addressed.
mpa-1.howto: When: On first opening the eyes, before touching the phone. Practice: Look once at whatever is actually there—ceiling, light, window. Recite the short invocation once, or the complete verse if learned. Return: Get up and attend to the day.
mpa-1.sign: Everyday integration: Get up and attend to the day.

_editorial.needs_check: The four-word pocket line is an excerpt from a longer verse; make that visible.

deha-1.brief: The body is called the deity’s temple, and one’s Self the enduring deity. This is a traditional maxim; its attribution as verse 1 of Abhinavagupta’s Dehasthadevatācakra is not supported by the checked witness.
deha-1.logic: Respect the body as a place of worship, including when tired, ordinary or uncomfortable.
deha-1.howto: When: While still in bed or just sitting up. Practice: Be aware of the whole body, without requiring it to feel calm or sacred. Say the half-verse slowly. Return: Stand, wash, and care for it.
deha-1.sign: Everyday integration: Stand, wash, and care for it.

_editorial.pocket_iast_candidate: deho devālayaḥ proktaḥ svātmā devaḥ sanātanaḥ
_editorial.needs_check: Keep as unattributed/traditional only if a publication-quality witness and rights are secured; otherwise replace with a genuinely sourced Dehastha verse.

mpa-10.brief: Waking, dreaming, and deep sleep are described as expressions of the Lord, who is nevertheless partless in reality.
mpa-10.logic: Recognise a change of state without needing to locate an additional permanent mental object.
mpa-10.howto: When: At the transition out of sleep. Practice: Name the state you have just left, then say the short clause “yet in truth you are without parts.” Return: Begin ordinary morning activity.
mpa-10.sign: Everyday integration: Begin ordinary morning activity.

_editorial.needs_check: Do not teach the waking/dreaming metaphor as empirical proof of metaphysical identity.

deha-6.brief: The hymn praises Ānandabhairavī, whose reflective awareness is linked with the world’s appearing, shining, and being relished.
deha-6.logic: What appears and the knowing of it can be contemplated together.
deha-6.howto: When: At dawn or the first visible change in daylight. Practice: Notice light arriving and recite the closing praise of the Goddess. No visualisation is necessary. Return: Open the curtains or leave the room.
deha-6.sign: Everyday integration: Open the curtains or leave the room.

_editorial.needs_check: Independent witness numbers this verse 5 rather than 6; use its reading udāya...līlāṃ, and collate the Sanskrit.

mpa-14.brief: The Lord is already stainless. Why would a bath purify the one who is beyond impurity?
mpa-14.logic: The water cares for a body, while the verse challenges the idea that the absolute needs cleaning.
mpa-14.howto: When: While washing hands or showering. Practice: Ask the rhetorical question once and wash normally. Return: Dry yourself and leave.
mpa-14.sign: Everyday integration: Dry yourself and leave.

_editorial.needs_check: Keep ritual paradox separate from ordinary hygiene; the passage is not advice to avoid washing.

sst-17-26.brief: May this body, nourished by devotion, become suitable for worship of You.
sst-17-26.logic: Devotion can be embodied as how the body is used in the next activity.
sst-17-26.howto: When: After bathing or getting dressed. Practice: Say the final petition while placing your hands at rest; no imposed gesture or pose. Return: Go do one useful thing.
sst-17-26.sign: Everyday integration: Go do one useful thing.

_editorial.needs_check: This is a genuine grammatical petition; suitable as a short recitation from the full verse.

mpa-17b.brief: What use is waving a lamp before the Lord who shines by himself? The verse questions the adequacy of outward ritual.
mpa-17b.logic: The gesture may train attention, rather than supply something missing to Śiva.
mpa-17b.howto: When: At the mirror, or when turning on a light. Practice: Say the question once. If using a lamp, do so safely; an imagined offering is optional. Return: Finish your washing or dressing.
mpa-17b.sign: Everyday integration: Finish your washing or dressing.

_editorial.needs_check: Second half’s Sanskrit reading needs witness collation; no claims of “chest-first brightening.”

mpa-19b.brief: The litany asks what gift, libation, dismissal or request for pardon could be offered to the complete, ever-content, all-pervading Lord.
mpa-19b.logic: A closing bow is not a transaction with a distant deity.
mpa-19b.howto: When: When ending a small devotional act. Practice: Read the complete verse slowly. Let its questions complete the ritual without adding another elaborate ending. Return: Put the towel or ritual item away.
mpa-19b.sign: Everyday integration: Put the towel or ritual item away.

_editorial.needs_check: Remove unusual avagraha in vyāpakasyāpratyakṣasya if the checked witness confirms; do not make up a mantra from a fragment.

bhair-7.brief: The poet describes speech as a Goddess and sense-objects as flowers of worship, followed by bowing and entering the heart.
bhair-7.logic: Treat words as something offered, and therefore worthy of care.
bhair-7.howto: When: Before a difficult conversation. Practice: Pause for one natural breath and read or recall the verse. Listen to the other person before deciding what to say. Return: Speak plainly rather than trying to sound mystical.
bhair-7.sign: Everyday integration: Speak plainly rather than trying to sound mystical.

_editorial.needs_check: Author Kṣemarāja, not Abhinavagupta; local L2 source omitted viṣayakusumakḷptārcaḥ although full text includes it.

anu-3.brief: The verse presents ordinary sound, bodily posture and breath in an expansive register: mantra, mudrā and yoga, when recognised in consciousness.
anu-3.logic: Notice that ordinary speaking is part of experience rather than outside spiritual life.
anu-3.howto: When: After saying something ordinary, not just before a formal chant. Practice: Recall the phrase once. Avoid turning it into permission for careless speech. Return: Return attention to the person present.
anu-3.sign: Everyday integration: Return attention to the person present.

_editorial.needs_check: Do not assert “every harmful statement is sanctified.” Anchor is a fragment and must be marked so.

mpa-8.brief: Enough of repeated discourse on distinctions. In the whole verse, the savour of devotion renders even the declaration “all is one” inadequate.
mpa-8.logic: Nonduality is not another argument that must be won.
mpa-8.howto: When: When a discussion becomes performative, especially a spiritual argument. Practice: Say the short phrase inwardly once. Listen and consider whether another explanation is useful. Return: Respond accurately if needed—or let the point rest.
mpa-8.sign: Everyday integration: Respond accurately if needed—or let the point rest.

_editorial.needs_check: Do not turn this into a ban on critical inquiry or difficult conversations.

pan-3.brief: The devotee complains that the Lord does not speak, look, listen or intervene—then recalls the scriptural denial of such bodily faculties.
pan-3.logic: Devotional address may include protest without pretending that silence has ceased.
pan-3.howto: When: When prayer feels unanswered. Practice: Read the complaint as a lament; do not force a cheerful reversal. Return: Make whatever real-world request for help is needed.
pan-3.sign: Everyday integration: Make whatever real-world request for help is needed.

_editorial.needs_check: Long metre; proofread all sandhi and translation from witness. Do not call the ending a compulsory joke.

mpa-20.brief: The verse calls for an understanding of unity, directing the mind toward the Lord across all conditions.
mpa-20.logic: Offering is not abandoning the task; careful work can embody devotion.
mpa-20.howto: When: Before opening a work task. Practice: Say the opening clause once: “Just so is the highest worship.” Choose the next concrete action. Return: Start the task and complete one small unit.
mpa-20.sign: Everyday integration: Start the task and complete one small unit.

_editorial.needs_check: The word aikyabuddhayā/aikyabuddhyā varies across transmissions and merits grammatical and source review; do not claim a sensory sign.

sst-1-14.brief: The verse invokes the teaching to worship Śiva having become Śiva, and examines devotion through nonduality.
sst-1-14.logic: The one who worships and the worshipped are contemplated as nonseparate.
sst-1-14.howto: When: When work seems incompatible with practice. Practice: Say the short injunction once before beginning. No need to pretend the work has changed substance. Return: Perform the ordinary task responsibly.
sst-1-14.sign: Everyday integration: Perform the ordinary task responsibly.

_editorial.needs_check: Since the surface has yajeteti, note restored word boundaries: yajet + iti.

deha-8.brief: The hymn represents ahaṃkṛti, I-making, as a goddess whose flowers of self-assertion worship Bhairava.
deha-8.logic: Even this mental movement is something to recognise and work with, not necessarily eradicate by force.
deha-8.howto: When: When pride, embarrassment or wanting credit becomes very conspicuous. Practice: Acknowledge that impulse without dramatizing it. Recite the praise of Śāmbhavī if learned. Return: Credit others fairly and continue.
deha-8.sign: Everyday integration: Credit others fairly and continue.

_editorial.needs_check: Independent witness numbers the verse 7, not 8. Avoid claims of solar-plexus heat or a literal internal fire.

mpa-9.brief: As the Lord’s own form expands, you, I, and the entire world appear; when it withdraws, these distinctions no longer appear.
mpa-9.logic: Experience need not be carried as though its totality were the private burden of one small self.
mpa-9.howto: When: When work becomes overwhelming. Practice: Say the short catalogue of “you, I, the whole world,” then name the next necessary task. Return: Do one thing at a time.
mpa-9.sign: Everyday integration: Do one thing at a time.

_editorial.needs_check: The selected short phrase is nominal and incomplete as an independent sentence. Label as remembered excerpt.

gita-424.brief: Offering-instrument, oblation, sacrificial fire, offerer and goal are all said to be Brahman. Lakshmanjoo reads this through Śiva.
gita-424.logic: Eating becomes an occasion to notice giver, gift and recipient in one field of awareness.
gita-424.howto: When: Before the first bite. Practice: Set down utensils. If following the taught custom, place a little clean water in the palm, recite the full verse, then eat. The short line is an optional memory cue, not a replacement prescribed by the Gītā. Return: Eat normally, gratefully and attentively.
gita-424.sign: Everyday integration: Eat normally, gratefully and attentively.

_editorial.needs_check: Identify Gītā original vs Abhinavagupta’s Gītā commentary vs Lakshmanjoo’s teaching. Water-in-palm practice belongs to a particular teaching, not the bare verse.

somananda.brief: The author asks Śiva, present as one’s own form and veiling himself through his own nature, to make an offering of homage to himself through his own power.
somananda.logic: The actor, the impediment and the addressed Lord are contemplated within Śiva’s self-relation.
somananda.howto: When: Before a meal, particularly if it follows Brahmārpaṇam. Practice: Read or say the complete verse. Do not turn it into a ritual to erase guilt on command. Return: Eat or return to the person sharing the meal.
somananda.sign: Everyday integration: Eat or return to the person sharing the meal.

_editorial.pocket_iast_candidate: śivaḥ karotu nijayā namaḥ śaktyā tatātmane
_editorial.needs_check: Use 1.1, not 7.103; fix padaccheda according to checked edition; the pocket is the closing half, not a standalone attested mantra.

deha-5.brief: The sense-goddesses constantly worship consciousness-filled Ānandabhairava with their enjoyment of their own objects, in the lotus of the heart.
deha-5.logic: A sense-experience can be understood as offering rather than as something outside spiritual practice.
deha-5.howto: When: At the first taste of food. Practice: Take one ordinary bite. Notice taste as taste, then recite the closing praise if desired. Return: Enjoy the meal without needing to intensify sensations.
deha-5.sign: Everyday integration: Enjoy the meal without needing to intensify sensations.

_editorial.needs_check: Independent witness assigns this Sanskrit to v.3, not v.5. No promise of warming chest or flavour enhancement.

sst-15-2.brief: The devotees are depicted as satisfied by consuming the very structures of limiting experience—māyā, time, necessity, attachment and the like.
sst-15-2.logic: What ordinarily binds can become material for recognition.
sst-15-2.howto: When: When desire or dissatisfaction accompanies a meal. Practice: Read the verse as a poetic vision; avoid turning ordinary eating into a literal ritual of consuming metaphysical categories. Return: Eat with care and attend to what is actually needed.
sst-15-2.sign: Everyday integration: Eat with care and attend to what is actually needed.

_editorial.needs_check: The “menu” is poetic and metaphysical, not a dietary instruction.

sst-16-8.brief: The speaker asks to remain in devotion whether troubled or at ease, weeping or laughing, solemn or unsettled.
sst-16-8.logic: Devotion need not depend on securing a pleasant state.
sst-16-8.howto: When: During travel, waiting or an unplanned interruption. Practice: Recite the whole verse in four short quarters if learned; first practise just the paired conditions. Return: Continue the wait without pretending to enjoy it.
sst-16-8.sign: Everyday integration: Continue the wait without pretending to enjoy it.

_editorial.needs_check: Opening alone is not a full prayer; printing the whole 32-syllable stanza is preferable.

sst-17-19.brief: The speaker longs to taste the joy of worship in every act, moment after moment.
sst-17-19.logic: A transition can be remembered as worship without needing to produce ecstasy.
sst-17-19.howto: When: Between ordinary activities. Practice: Say the small temporal phrase, or the entire prayer when it is memorised. Pause for one ordinary breath. Return: Move to the next action.
sst-17-19.sign: Everyday integration: Move to the next action.

_editorial.needs_check: Excerpt means “in every action, moment by moment,” but is not a complete prayer.

anu-2b.brief: The verse challenges the assumed reality of bondage, ending with an invitation to stop grasping and rejecting.
anu-2b.logic: Let experience appear without the immediate demand to keep or eliminate it.
anu-2b.howto: When: In a queue, during uncertainty, or when scrolling compulsively. Practice: Say the two prohibitions once. Unclench a hand only if it helps; no ritual hand movement is required. Return: Choose the next sensible action.
anu-2b.sign: Everyday integration: Choose the next sensible action.

_editorial.needs_check: Non-grasping is not advice to avoid necessary safety or ethical decisions.

sst-16-1.brief: The hymn opens an inquiry into concealment: what hides Śiva for ordinary consciousness and what does not hide him for the devotee?
sst-16-1.logic: Distinguish the apparent obscuring condition from the object itself.
sst-16-1.howto: When: When caught in a habitual interpretation that blocks a fresh look. Practice: Do not publish a recitation until the complete Sanskrit has been collated. For now use the English question as a study reflection. Return: Look again at the actual situation.
sst-16-1.sign: Everyday integration: Look again at the actual situation.

_editorial.needs_check: CRITICAL: current corpus snippet is incomplete. Prior paraphrase “two classes of people” is not a literal rendering of the surviving text.

bh-3.brief: When the Lord is recognised as the all-pervading Self, fear of repeated worldly existence is denied, even while difficult karma and suffering may remain.
bh-3.logic: The verse speaks to a metaphysical fear; it does not deny bodily pain or replace treatment.
bh-3.howto: When: When unwell or frightened by what might happen. Practice: Recite the short reassurance, or the full verse if it is familiar. Name the specific practical need separately. Return: Rest, seek care, or ask someone for help as needed.
bh-3.sign: Everyday integration: Rest, seek care, or ask someone for help as needed.

_editorial.needs_check: Avoid promising that mantra removes illness or panic.

pan-5.brief: The speaker acknowledges that, even after divine assistance, he keeps forgetting the Lord. The prayer becomes a candid plea rather than a display of attainment.
pan-5.logic: Forgetting need not prevent another act of devotion.
pan-5.howto: When: When exhausted, ill or spiritually discouraged. Practice: Read as much of the complete verse as is accessible. The short phrase “I indeed forget you” can be remembered as a confession, not as a separately transmitted mantra. Return: Take medicine, rest or reconnect with someone if needed.
pan-5.sign: Everyday integration: Take medicine, rest or reconnect with someone if needed.

_editorial.needs_check: Long Sanskrit contains suspicious forms in current transcription; collate before shipping.

sst-5-2.brief: Utpaladeva asks when the dust of the Lord’s lotus feet will adorn him and he will dance in overflowing joy.
sst-5-2.logic: Longing itself is part of devotion; inability to dance is not a failure.
sst-5-2.howto: When: When bodily limitations make joy feel far away. Practice: Read it as an open question rather than a demand for immediate transformation. Return: Make room for whatever care the body needs.
sst-5-2.sign: Everyday integration: Make room for whatever care the body needs.

_editorial.needs_check: Keep the verse complete rather than invent a supposedly therapeutic short charm.

mpa-3.brief: The seeker looks inward for the Self and does not find it as an object; what is seen is nevertheless affirmed as the Lord’s appearance.
mpa-3.logic: The contemplative claim is about recognition, not proof that pain is imaginary.
mpa-3.howto: When: When the body or circumstances feel alien. Practice: Look at one ordinary thing and recite the final clause if learned. Return: Attend to the condition or task directly.
mpa-3.sign: Everyday integration: Attend to the condition or task directly.

_editorial.pocket_iast_candidate: yac ca dṛṣṭaṃ tvam eva tat
_editorial.needs_check: Restore and verify sandhi from the full text before printing a standalone excerpt.

mpa-11.brief: The verse relates waking and dissolution to the Lord, and concludes that the entire world is of that nature.
mpa-11.logic: The day can be released without demanding to control the night.
mpa-11.howto: When: Just before sleep. Practice: Recall the short conclusion once. No breath manipulation or effort to remain aware through sleep is required. Return: Turn off the light and sleep.
mpa-11.sign: Everyday integration: Turn off the light and sleep.

_editorial.needs_check: The selected form is a segmented padaccheda, not a claim of a standalone mantra.

vbt-75.brief: When sleep is approaching and outward objects fade, the verse presents that transitional condition as a place where the supreme Goddess shines.
vbt-75.logic: The movement toward sleep can be included in awareness.
vbt-75.howto: When: As drowsiness naturally comes. Practice: Read the verse earlier if necessary; at bedtime simply notice the transition without fighting to keep it. Return: Allow sleep to arrive.
vbt-75.sign: Everyday integration: Allow sleep to arrive.

_editorial.needs_check: Do not urge practitioners to induce dissociation, sleep loss or unusual visual experiences.

sst-9-14.brief: Utpaladeva longs to rest at the cool lotus feet of the Lord within a condition of fullness and intimacy.
sst-9-14.logic: Devotional rest can be imagined without treating the image as a literal bodily event.
sst-9-14.howto: When: When lying down to sleep. Practice: Read the full verse slowly; allow the imagery of cooling and rest to remain poetic. Return: Let attention turn away from the day.
sst-9-14.sign: Everyday integration: Let attention turn away from the day.

_editorial.needs_check: Current compound aśeṣaviṣayāśūnya... does not support the summary “free from every object”; collate with full commentary.

anu-4b.brief: The verse distinguishes the joy of nondual recognition from possession, intoxication and sensory splendour, likening recognition to recovering a forgotten treasure and lowering a burden.
anu-4b.logic: A teaching about intrinsic fullness can be contemplated alongside the fatigue that is actually present.
anu-4b.howto: When: When looking back over an exhausting day. Practice: Read the passage as a comparison. Do not demand bliss before being permitted to sleep. Return: Rest.
